accepted.question_text: For suitable perturbations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0 on the real line and suitable almost periodic initial data u_0(x), does the Cauchy problem have a unique global solution u(x,t) that evolves almost periodically in time?

evidence.quote: It is a natural, open and very challenging conjecture that the result of Damanik et al. remains true for (suitable) perturbations of KdV, i.e., for (suitable) perturbations of KdV, the Cauchy problem with (suitable) almost periodic initial data u0 (x), has a unique global solution u(x, t), which evolves almost periodically in time.

accepted.question_text: For random n x n band matrices H with bandwidth w <= n and independent entries H_ij inside the band, can one prove the Fyodorov-Mirlin conjecture that the local eigenvalue statistics are in the GUE universality class when w is much larger than sqrt(n), but become Poisson when w is much smaller than sqrt(n), in both the real symmetric and complex Hermitian settings?

evidence.quote: An open problem of great, ongoing interest is the question of the behavior of random n x n band matrices H with bandwidth w <= n, H_ij = 0 if |i - j| >= w. The long-standing conjecture of V. Fyodorov and A. Mirlin [59] from 1991 is that for iid H_ij, |i - j| < w, with w >> sqrt(n), the local statistics of the eigenvalues of H are GUE, but for w << sqrt(n), the behavior is Poisson.

accepted.question_text: For random Schrodinger operators H = -Delta + V with random potential V, can one rigorously analyze the bulk spectral regime where eigenfunctions are expected to delocalize and eigenvalues are expected to follow random-matrix statistics, and can one construct and analyze models that exhibit the conjectured transition from Poisson statistics to random-matrix statistics at a mobility edge?

evidence.quote: Perhaps the most challenging problem currently in the spectral theory of Schrodinger operators H = -Delta + V, Delta = Laplacian, is to analyze the spectrum of H when V is a random function. There is also believed to be a so-called mobility edge mu in the spectrum at which the statistics switch from a Poisson distribution to a random matrix distribution. So far this conjecture is wide open. It is of interest to construct and analyze models where such a transition, Poisson -> random matrix statistics, takes place.

accepted.question_text: For Wigner ensembles whose equilibrium measure is supported on more than one interval, can one prove universality in the bulk and at all spectral edges, and can one also analyze parameter regimes in which intervals in the support of the equilibrium measure open and close?

evidence.quote: Another open problem in RMT is to prove universality, in the bulk and at (all) the edges, for Wigner ensembles in the case that the equilibrium measure for the ensemble is supported on more than one interval. Furthermore, one would like to analyze and control situations where parameters in the underlying matrix distributions vary, and intervals in the support of the equilibrium distribution for the ensemble open and close.

accepted.question_text: For random-matrix models that depend on external parameters p and undergo critical changes in the support of the equilibrium measure at values p_c, can one rigorously analyze the corresponding double-scaling and more general multi-scaling limits in which p approaches p_c while the matrix size n tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: In RMT almost all problems involve matrix distributions which depend on some external parameters, say p. Typically there are critical values p_c at which the nature of the equilibrium measure for the ensemble changes. The double-scaling problems, p -> p_c and matrix size n -> infinity, are of basic interest. Most of these problems remain open.

accepted.question_text: Can one obtain rigorous explicit formulas for Tracy-Widom distribution functions for general beta-ensembles beyond the classical invariant cases beta = 1, 2, and 4, including a rigorous completion of Rumanov's approach for all even beta > 0 and a rigorous verification of the asymptotic formulas proposed by Borot, Eynard, Majumdar, and Nadal for general beta > 0?

evidence.quote: An open problem of long-standing interest concerns explicit formulae for the Tracy-Widom distribution functions for general beta-ensembles. It is of great interest to complete Rumanov's analysis rigorously, not only for beta = 6, but for all even beta > 0. It is a challenging open problem to verify rigorously these formulae of Borot et al.

accepted.question_text: For the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation with general initial data, can one prove full 3:2:1 KPZ universality in the strong sense proposed by Corwin, Quastel, and Remenik for solutions of the Cauchy problem, and can one identify the limiting process that arises in that scaling limit?

evidence.quote: The most challenging open problem regarding the KPZ equation is to prove 3 : 2 : 1 KPZ universality in the strong sense of Corwin, Quastel and Remenik [30] alluded to above, for solutions of the Cauchy problem of the KPZ equation for a wide set of initial data, and to identify the limiting process.

accepted.question_text: Can one analyze solutions of the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation simultaneously at more than one space-time point, rather than only through one-point statistics?

evidence.quote: Another open problem is to analyze solutions of KPZ at more than one space-time point.

accepted.question_text: For last-passage percolation with general weights, can one prove the full 3:2:1 KPZ scaling law, meaning time scale 3, spatial-correlation scale 2, and fluctuation scale 1 in the KPZ normalization?

evidence.quote: However, many basic problems remain open. In particular showing that LPP with general weights has 3 : 2 : 1 scaling, is far from being resolved.

accepted.question_text: For the longest increasing subsequence problem, can one prove KPZ-class fluctuation results when the permutation is sampled from distributions more general than the uniform distribution?

evidence.quote: Also, regarding the original longest increasing subsequence problem, KPZ universality for the fluctuations has been proved so far only for the uniform distribution on the permutations: The problem for the fluctuations with more general distributions is very much open.

accepted.question_text: Can one explain the mechanism behind Tracy and Widom's solution of the asymmetric simple exclusion process with step initial data, and extend that method to more general initial data sets?

evidence.quote: In another direction, it remains an open, and somewhat mysterious, problem to understand how Tracy and Widom's solution of ASEP actually "works", and to extend their method of solution to more general initial data.

accepted.question_text: Can one develop a perturbation theory for non-solvable KPZ-type interacting-particle models that plays a role analogous to KAM theory in integrable dynamical systems, so that persistence of integrability-like structure and robustness of asymptotic scaling phenomena can be studied beyond exactly solvable models?

evidence.quote: In addition, it is particularly frustrating that there is no known perturbation theory, analogous to KAM theory for integrable dynamical systems, that one can use to investigate the persistence of "integrability" for non-solvable models and demonstrate robustness for asymptotic scaling phenomena. Developing such a perturbation theory is an open conceptual and technical problem of the first order.

accepted.question_text: For the Toda algorithm applied to random Hermitian matrices, where the stopping time T^(1)(H) is used to compute the largest eigenvalue, can one prove universality for the centered and scaled stopping-time variable in the cases of beta = 1 invariant ensembles and beta = 1 or 2 Wigner ensembles?

evidence.quote: Thus the Toda algorithm with stopping time T (1) (H) is an algorithm to compute the largest eigenvalue of a given matrix H.

In order to prove universality for the centered and scaled variable T (1) - <T (1)> / sigma_T (1) (cf. tau_{epsilon,n,A,E} at the beginning of this section) one needs to control the statistics of the lambda_j's and the beta_k's as in (8), (9) jointly as n -> infinity. For beta = 2 invariant ensembles, this can be done, but for beta = 1 invariant ensembles, and for beta = 1 or 2 WE's, this problem is still very much open.

accepted.question_text: For the QR algorithm applied to random matrices, can one control, as n tends to infinity, the bulk eigenvalue-ratio statistics |lambda_{j+1}/lambda_j| and |lambda_{j-1}/lambda_j| near the eigenvalue lambda_j closest to zero, together with the associated normalized eigenvectors, so as to prove the analogue of the Toda-algorithm universality theorem for QR?

evidence.quote: It is very much an open problem to control, as n -> infinity, the statistics of |lambda_{j+1}/lambda_j|, |lambda_{j-1}/lambda_j| for lambda_j ~ 0 deep in the bulk of the spectrum, together with their associated normalized eigenvectors, as in (8), (9). The QR algorithm is the "go to" algorithm for eigenvalue computation, and the proof of the analog of Theorem 1 for the QR algorithm is an open problem of great interest.

accepted.question_text: For some eigenvalue algorithm A, can one prove a universality theorem for the deflation time T_{epsilon,n,A,E}, where T_{epsilon,n,A,E} is the smallest time at which the evolving matrix becomes approximately block diagonal to accuracy epsilon and the problem depends on statistics of both eigenvalues and eigenvectors?

evidence.quote: The most challenging problem for eigenvalue computation with random data is to prove the analog of Theorem 1 for the deflation time T_{epsilon,n,A,E} for some algorithm A.
Indeed, T_{epsilon,n,A,E} is the smallest time t for which X(t) has the block form A B; B^* C where A is j x j, C is (n - j) x (n - j) and ||B|| = ||B^*|| <= epsilon for some 1 <= j <= n - 1.

accepted.question_text: Can one rigorously prove universality for one of the other numerical algorithms with random data discussed in the paper, especially the conjugate-gradient algorithm for solving a random linear system A x = b with both A and b random?

evidence.quote: It is an interesting and challenging open problem to prove universality rigorously for any of the other numerical algorithms discussed in [40]. The conjugate gradient algorithm, in particular, to compute the solution of the linear system Ax = b with A and b random, seems to be "within reach".

accepted.question_text: Can the orthogonal-polynomial-based sampling method developed by Olver, Nadakuditi, and Trogdon for invariant unitary ensembles be extended to orthogonal and symplectic invariant ensembles, while retaining its essentially machine-accuracy sampling behavior?

evidence.quote: While the method of Li and Menon is significantly faster, the method of Olver et al. samples the distribution to essentially machine accuracy, a task which is computationally impractical using Dyson Brownian motion. It is an open problem to extend the method of S. Olver et al. to orthogonal and symplectic invariant ensembles.

accepted.question_text: For the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the half-line, i u_t = u_{xx} + 2 |u|^2 u for x >= 0 and t >= 0, with prescribed initial data u(x,0) = f(x) and oscillatory boundary forcing u(0,t) = e^{i w t}, can one compute the long-time asymptotic behavior of the solution u(x,t) for general real driving frequency w?

evidence.quote: A particular stand out open problem is to compute the long-time behavior of the solution u(x, t) of the focusing NLS equation, iut = uxx + 2|u|2 u, with u(x, 0) = f(x), x >= 0, given and u(0, t) = e^{iwt}, t >= 0 with w in R.

accepted.question_text: For the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the half-line with oscillatory boundary forcing u(0,t) = e^{i w t}, can one show that as w decreases toward 0 the boundary drive excites k-gap solutions of periodic NLS?

evidence.quote: We expect similar behavior for focusing NLS, with k-gap solutions of periodic NLS emerging from the driver e^{iwt} as w downarrow 0. This is an open problem of the first order, illustrating how the natural modes of an extended physical system (k-gap solutions in the case of NLS) can be excited by driving the system externally at one end.

accepted.question_text: Can the Bikbaev-Tarasov Backlund-transform method be adapted to solve the initial-boundary value problem for the defocusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation i u_t = u_{xx} - 2 |u|^2 u on the half-line with Robin boundary condition u_x(0,t) + q u(0,t) = 0, despite the singularities introduced when the solution is extended from x > 0 to x < 0?

evidence.quote: It is an interesting open problem to use the Bikbaev-Tarasov method to solve the IBVP for defocusing NLS, iut = uxx - 2|u|2 u, with Robin boundary conditions at x = 0. In this case the Backlund transformation extending the solution from x > 0 to x < 0 introduces certain singularities which must be controlled and the long-time behavior of the solution of the IBVP will be very different from the case of focusing NLS.

accepted.question_text: For the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the half-line with Robin boundary conditions and smooth matching initial and boundary data, can one prove that the initial-boundary value problem remains classical in x > 0 and t > 0 for a general class of smooth nonlinearities, rather than relying on the special Backlund-transform structure available only for the cubic focusing case?

evidence.quote: So the open problem here is a PDE problem, viz., to prove that the IPVP for NLS with a general class of non-linearities, with Robin boundary conditions and matching, smooth initial data, is classical in x > 0, t > 0.

accepted.question_text: More generally, what smoothness can be proved for solutions of initial-boundary value problems for dispersive equations in arbitrary spatial dimension?

evidence.quote: Much more generally, the open problem is to understand what can be said about smoothness of solutions of IBVP's for dispersive equations in any dimension. This problem seems to be largely unexplored.

accepted.question_text: For the semiclassical focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation, can one solve the forward scattering problem for general smooth initial data and then implement the associated Riemann-Hilbert numerical methodology to compute the Cauchy problem in the small-dispersion limit epsilon = hbar down to 0?

evidence.quote: It remains an open problem (see [34]) to solve the forward problem for focusing NLS with general smooth initial data, and then implement the RHP methodology, to obtain the solution of the Cauchy problem in the small dispersion limit epsilon = hbar downarrow 0.

accepted.question_text: For the Airy integral operator A_s on L^2(s, infinity), whose Fredholm determinant gives the edge-scaling distribution for the largest GUE eigenvalue, can one analyze the eigenfunctions u_tilde_j(s) asymptotically as s tends to infinity and also compute them accurately for finite s?

evidence.quote: It is an open problem to analyze the behavior of the eigenfunctions u_tilde_j(s) as s -> infinity, and to compute their behavior for finite s.

accepted.question_text: For perturbations of the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation of the form i u_tilde_t + u_tilde_xx + 2 |u_tilde|^2 u_tilde + epsilon |u_tilde|^ell u_tilde = 0 with decaying initial data, can one analyze the long-time behavior of solutions, especially in the case where the initial data correspond to a two-soliton solution of the unperturbed focusing NLS equation?

evidence.quote: An open problem of great and basic interest is to analyze solutions of the Cauchy problem for perturbations of the focusing NLS equation.
Of particular interest is the case where f_tilde(x) corresponds to a 2-soliton solution for (unperturbed) focusing NLS.

accepted.question_text: Can one use Riemann-Hilbert and nonlinear steepest-descent methods to give a fully rigorous proof of the asymptotic results obtained by Venakides, Deift, and Oba for the Toda shock problem, where the driven lattice settles into a one-gap periodic state for sufficiently strong driving?

evidence.quote: The proof of this result, however, was not fully rigorous. There are two open problems here. The first is to use Riemann-Hilbert/steepest-descent methods to prove the results in Venakides et al. rigorously.

accepted.question_text: If the exponential interaction in the Toda shock problem is replaced by a nearby force law F(x) so that the lattice equation becomes x_doubleprime_k = F(x_{k-1} - x_k) - F(x_k - x_{k+1}), can one analyze the general shock problem for suitably small perturbations F(x) of e^x and prove the numerically observed asymptotic behavior?

evidence.quote: The second problem concerns the fact that if we replace the exponential forces e^x by a general force F(x), x_doubleprime_k = F(x_{k-1} - x_k) - F(x_k - x_{k+1}), then numerical simulations show that the solution of the shock problem for this system behaves in the same way as t -> infinity as the Toda system, provided (15) has a 2-periodic solution x_k(t + T) = x_k(t), x_{k+2}(t) = x_k(t) for k in Z.
Second open problem: Analyze the general shock problem (15) for suitably small perturbations F(x) of e^x.

accepted.question_text: Can one give a rigorous and explicit mathematical solution of the diffraction problem for waves passing through two finite slits in the plane, the setting underlying Young's double-slit experiment in optics and the analogous double-slit experiment in quantum mechanics?

evidence.quote: However the rigorous solution of the problem of diffraction from two slits remains open. This problem is of great mathematical and physical importance, describing as it does Young's famous double slit experiment in optics, and the double slit experiment in quantum mechanics.
